chapter_theme: ஞானம் - 5, thirteen stanzas the author says Siva gave him as guru: the kalpa that gives deathlessness is not in distant mountains but in the body, where the serpent's head, the undying breath and the black-gooseberry juice are found; the house of turiya is Valai, the goddess, whose feet alone are to be worshipped at the suzhumunai; and the letters of Om (a, u, m and the one letter) are mapped onto pati, pasu, the Supreme, the channels and the nada-bindu. Seeing the holy dance in the body is release and siddhi, and the knower of the one letter is the only guru.
structure_note: Thirteen stanzas chaining by antadi (கூடே / கூடப்பா; சித்தியாமே / ஆமென்ற; பாடினேனே / பாடுகின்ற; ஊணிப்பாரே / ஊணியதோர்; துறந்திட்டேனே / துறந்திட்டேனே; and so on to குருவாக). 2442 to 2444 give the inner kalpa, Valai and her worship; 2445 to 2447 the letters of Om and the central nadi; 2448 to 2450 the mind at the suzhumunai, the Devi and the Omkara pillar; 2451 to 2453 who the guru is; 2454 closes with the count of thirteen and a curse on mockers.

2442.reading: For the kalpa you need not go far, nor wander the peaks of stone mountains; standing on the head of the serpent called the naga, find the undying breath, climb to the tip, stand in a mind made firm by resolve, and see the true juice of the black gooseberry; if you drop it as a small thing you will wander lost; go and join the Supreme called turiya.
2442.nuance: கற்பம் is the rejuvenating herb or preparation of Siddha medicine; the verse says it is not gathered in the mountains but found within. The sense turns on cipher: tradition takes the serpent as kundalini at the base, சாகாத கால் (the undying foot or breath) as the breath that does not go out, and கருநெல்லிச் சாறு (black-gooseberry juice) as the nectar from the head; Kakapusundar uses the same herb-name for the deathless state. A plain medical reading, that gooseberry juice is the kalpa, is also possible and the verse plays on both.

2443.reading: Join it: the house of turiya is Valai, and they call her Nathar-Maheswari, hard to describe; seek her alone and worship her; the beauty Nandi speaks of will appear and appear; everything up to the sikara boundary will appear; the flood of nectar called the mute will spring; seek this, this is the thing to seek; this alone is siddhi in the world.
2443.nuance: வாலை, the girl-goddess of the Siddhars' cult, is here identified with the turiya state itself and with Maheswari, so that worship of her is entry into the fourth state. சிகாரவரை, the boundary of the sikara, may be the crown of the head or the letter சி of the five-letter mantra; ஊமையென்ற அமிர்தவெள்ளம், the mute nectar flood, is the nectar of the yogic tradition. The verse makes this inner worship the only siddhi.

2444.reading: See the fullness called 'Aum' at the suzhumunai; the fair standing of bindu they see in the moon; the hum 'Om' is at the centre of the brows, noble one, and is seen in the house called the bow; worship her feet called 'Vam'; nothing else is worship, my son, I have said it; the Supreme called 'Pam' is the first letter; I have sung Vedanta, I have sung.
2444.nuance: The verse places seed-syllables (ஆம், ஓம், வாம், பாம்) at body-places: the suzhumunai, the moon (the left channel or the head), the brow centre and the 'bow' (the arched brows). Only the worship of 'her feet' (Valai's, from 2443) is worship, a claim as exclusive as the Tirumanthiram's inclusive lists of lingam materials. பாமென்ற பரமனல்லோ முதலெழுத்தாம் is read by tradition as 'the Supreme is the first letter, a'; the syllable itself is unexplained.

2445.reading: All that is sung is pati; the letter that stands in pati is 'a'; the Supreme that is sought is the Omkara; the pasu of great good is 'u'; the suzhumunai that endures is the stream; the idaikalai that stood is nada-bindu; this is the Omkara science that moves through; fix and see the rare letter of light.
2445.nuance: The verse maps the letters of Om onto the Saiva categories: 'a' is pati, 'u' is pasu, Om as a whole is the Supreme, and the body's channels are the stream (தாரை) and nada-bindu. ஓங்கார வித்தை, the Omkara science, is the name it gives to this mapping. The third letter, 'm', is not assigned here, which may be deliberate (the one letter of 2453) or a gap.

2446.reading: There is an Omkara higher than the one fixed; noble one, there is glory, fix and see; the central nadi that is the pin kindles in the middle; all the wondrous letters stand contained there; it stands as a ladder, the five houses; see that letter which has become solitary; that house appears like a boat; I will tell no one, I have renounced it.
2446.nuance: அஞ்சு வீடு, the five houses on a ladder, is read by tradition as the five lower centres climbed by the central nadi; the boat-like house is unexplained, perhaps the crescent at the brow. சொல்லாதே ஒருவருக்குந் துறந்திட்டேனே is either 'do not tell anyone; I have renounced it' or 'I have renounced telling it to anyone', and the antadi carries துறந்திட்டேனே into 2447, where the author does go on telling.

2447.reading: I have renounced it: see the upper root and the lower root; with care fix and see the middle state; I have declared it: see the middle root and the middle nadi; then the stream that strikes the boundary appears; the five who dwell there are seen dancing; light-space and the sound of anklets are seen as one; the full pooranam too is this; see the true great light steadily.
2447.nuance: The upper, lower and middle roots (மூலம்) are the body's centres in cipher, and the five who dance may be the five elements or the five acts. சிலம்பொலி, the sound of anklets, is the dance of Siva heard within, which 2451 and 2453 name as the holy dance whose seeing is release. The verse identifies pooranam with this seen light and heard sound, giving the term of ஞானம் - 4 an experiential content.

2448.reading: As you simply look, drive the mind to the suzhumunai and see the breath there; subside, saying 'Mother, you are the Devi', and see; then come kaya-siddhi and yoga-siddhi; 'Um-ma' and 'Am-ma' are seen there; with one mind plant the mind at the suzhumunai; we have told all that was made by us; among the Nathars no one sings this.
2448.nuance: காயசித்தி, the perfected body, and யோகசித்தி are the two fruits claimed, and the means is the simplest the run offers: look, fix the mind, see the breath (கால்), address the Devi. உம்மாவும் அம்மாவும் may be two syllables (u-ma, a-ma) or the mother's two names; the text does not say. 'None of the Nathars sings this' claims the teaching goes beyond the Natha lineage.

2449.reading: In the Omkara circle that is seen a little fire rises and a smarting appears in the eye; in the idaikalai that is worn it dances like the Supreme; the wicked body melts away; all the anavams perish; the non-dual turiya dance stands dancing; all the fixed letters become the Devi; the Omkara pillar is awareness itself.
2449.nuance: The verse describes signs of practice (fire, smarting in the eye, the body melting) and makes the goal the destruction of ஆணவம், the ego-impurity, and the turiya dance that is non-dual (அத்துவிதம்). ஓங்காரக் கம்பம், the Omkara pillar, is the central channel as in the Thirumular Njanam's கம்பம்; here it is awareness (உணர்வு), which the antadi carries into 2450.

2450.reading: As for awareness: climb into the moon and spread, run and stand there in the letter called the head; the atom is the house, Siva is the crown; 'a' and pati are the subtle; the knot is the bow-brow, the boundless street; what is called Kailasa is the house of the Supreme; see the fire of the sun called the particle, and sleep, sleep at the pillar called the nape.
2450.nuance: A string of body-place glosses in cipher: the moon (head or left channel), the head-letter, the atom-house, the bow-brow, Kailasa, the sun's fire and the nape-pillar. Tradition reads them as the stations of the breath from the brow to the crown; the verse offers them as definitions (என்ன ... ஆகும்) without a key. 'Sleep at the pillar of the nape' is the turiya sleep of 2432.

2451.reading: He who knows and tells the root that became the three letters and the two letters is the guru; it is within the letter 'oo'; he who has seen awareness itself and known it is the teacher; 'no one knows, we have known', say each of the fools who do not know; the gods with Vishnu and Brahma sought and did not see; seeing the holy dance is release and siddhi.
2451.nuance: The three letters are a, u, m and the two letters are the pair of 2452 (root and seed, or Siva and Shakti); the root behind them is what the guru knows. ஊவெழுத்து (the letter 'oo') is unexplained and may be corrupt for ஓ or உ. The refrain திருநடனங் காண முத்தி சித்தியாமே closes 2451 and 2453, making the inner dance the one test.

2452.reading: The two letters and the one letter, standing there as the ajapa that moves within the root; with the root letter and the seed letter both, it sprouts from the seed and stands shining; fix the fine letter, mount the good vaasi, cross the street and the road to the jewelled hall, and look to the Supreme that is the inner meaning of the letter: to those who reach it, it gives siddhi and release.
2452.nuance: அசபை is the ajapa, the unrecited mantra of the breath (hamsa), which the verse places in the root centre. வாசி ஏறி, mounting the vaasi, uses the Siddhars' pun on breath and horse: the breath is ridden up the channel to the மணிமண்டபம், the jewelled hall at the crown. The 'inner meaning of the letter' is the Supreme, so the letter is a vehicle and not the goal.

2453.reading: No one in this world has seen the fruit of the one letter called Ekam and expounded it; those who have learned the Agamas and many books and say 'we have known' and 'silence': ask such a one quickly about the unboiled, undying head and foot; he who tells what was left out is the teacher; he who sees the one letter in the body is the jnani; seeing the holy dance is release and siddhi.
2453.nuance: The test of a teacher is a riddle: வேகாச் சாகாத் தலைகால், the head and foot that are not boiled and do not die, which tradition takes as the breath (கால்) and the head (the crown) kept deathless, as in 2442's சாகாத கால். Those who learned the Agamas and claim knowledge or silence cannot answer it. ஏகமெனு மோரெழுத்து, the one letter called Ekam, is the single letter beyond the three, the Omkara of 2446.

2454.reading: The rare knowledge that Uma's consort gave me as guru I have told as meaning in thirteen; if you know the meaning, pooranam too will fit and be seen; those who mock this book without grace will reach dire hell and live as ghosts; those who examine it with grace may know the state in which the sky stands.
2454.nuance: பத்தின் மூன்று, ten and three, matches the run's thirteen units. The closing curse on mockers and promise to examiners is conventional, but the promise is characteristic: not heaven but ஆகாயம் நின்ற நிலை, the state where space stands, the open void of 2411. Siva (Uma's consort) is named as the author's own guru, which grounds the run's repeated question of who the true guru is.

links.note: Kakapusundar tells the disciple to pluck and eat the black gooseberry, which becomes the unboiled head, and to hold the white snake, which is the undying breath; Agasthiyar tells him to stand on the serpent's head, find the undying breath and see the true black-gooseberry juice. The same three cipher images (gooseberry, serpent, undying foot) for the inner kalpa.

Tirumular drives bindu and nada upward along the marked path and drinks the nectar that is milk; Agasthiyar climbs from the serpent's head to the tip and sees the true juice of the black gooseberry. Both make the deathless substance something found by ascent within the body, and both warn that it is lost by letting go.

Sattaimuni tells the disciple to learn Valai's three letters and worship her, then Tripura's eight, Bhuvanai's and Yamalai's; Agasthiyar says the house of turiya is Valai, Nathar-Maheswari, and that she alone is to be worshipped. Both make Valai the object of the inner worship; Agasthiyar identifies her with the fourth state itself.

The Kural opens with 'a' as the first of letters and the Primal Lord as first of the world; Agasthiyar closes 2444 with the Supreme as the first letter. The image of God as the first letter is shared; the Kural uses it as a simile, Agasthiyar as an identity within the Omkara science of 2445.

Tirumular says that by one letter he became everything, by two he joined as two, by three the light springs up; Agasthiyar maps 'a' to pati, 'u' to pasu and Om to the Supreme, and tells the disciple to see the letter of light. Both read the letters of Om as the stages of the Lord's manifestation; Agasthiyar's mapping is onto the Siddhanta categories, Tirumular's onto the world.

Arunagirinathar asks to hold the serpent-like breath, see the pure light, plunge into the space above and see the vel and peacock shining there; Agasthiyar says that when the middle nadi is fixed the stream appears, the five dance, and light-space and the sound of anklets are seen as one. Both make the inner light and the vision in the upper space the fruit of the held breath.

2418 says that when nada becomes the guru you yourself become the guru who is beginning and end; 2451 says the guru is he who knows and tells the root that became the three and the two letters, and that the fools who say 'we have known' and even the gods have not seen it. The later run turns the inner-guru claim into a test for judging teachers.

Sivavakkiyar mounts the vaasi on the silent five letters and enters the light-filled sphere, where he and the Lord mingle until neither remains; Agasthiyar fixes the fine letter, mounts the good vaasi, crosses to the jewelled hall and looks to the Supreme that is the letter's inner meaning. The same ride of the breath on a mantra to the crown, with release as its fruit.

Tirumular says that though the Agamas are gathered in countless crores, without the knowledge the Lord declared they are writing on water; Agasthiyar says those who have learned the Agamas and many books and claim knowledge cannot answer for the undying head and foot, and only he who sees the one letter in the body is the jnani. Both deny that learning the Agamas is knowing.

The Kural asks what learning has achieved if the learned do not bow at the feet of the one of pure knowledge; Agasthiyar asks what the learners of the Agamas and many books know if they cannot tell the undying head and foot. Both measure learning by a knowledge it does not itself contain.

Tirumular says those who grieved the ascetics who taught the one-syllable mantra will be born as outcast dogs in a hundred forms; Agasthiyar says those who mock this book will live as ghosts in dire hell. The same closing curse on those who slight the teaching of the one letter; Tirumular's punishment is rebirth, Agasthiyar's is hell.

source_issues: 2446 line 1 மேல்முலங் is a misprint for மேல்மூலம் (upper root).
2451 line 3 ஊவெழுத்து (the letter 'oo') is unexplained and may be corrupt for ஓவெழுத்து or உவ்வெழுத்து.
2453 line 4 அறிந்தமென்பார் (for அறிந்தோமென்பார்) and line 7 ஒரெழுத்தை (for ஓரெழுத்தை) are misprints.
2454 says the run was told in thirteen (பத்தின் மூன்று); the run has thirteen units, so the count is consistent.
